correctness.rationale: Every closed-neighborhood facet is F_v together with one same-color vertex in each neighboring fiber. Girth >=5 guarantees that two different off-fiber vertices identify their unique generator. Pair each such face not containing pivot (v,a) with its extension by that pivot, descending in face size; all pairs are disjoint and all lower faces are free when removed. Exactly m 2^(m-1) sum_v(2^deg(v)-deg(v)-1) pairs are removed. The residual is the union of blocks P_uv=Delta(F_u)*D_v union D_u*Delta(F_v); each is a suspension of K_m,m, hence a wedge of (m-1)^2 two-spheres. The block assembly has contractible fiber intersections with incidence graph H, proving H wedge e(m-1)^2 two-spheres integrally. A fixed-color H subgraph is a section of the simplicial projection, so first-homology surjectivity and free-kernel rank follow from exact graph Euler characteristic. The embedded standard-library code exhaustively validates removals, residual faces, and independent F2 chain ranks for paths, stars, cycles and Petersen, widths 2,3,4. Only widths m>=3 are new; computations supplement, not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete all-parameter integral homotopy classification over arbitrary finite high-girth base graphs and nontrivial clique fiber widths, with explicit elementary simplicial collapse count and the exact first Čech persistence kernel. Local second-homology contribution scales quadratically with fiber width, distinguishing this construction from width-two prisms and from the previously classified Rips filtration. Branching trees, multiple-cycle bases, and cyclic strips are covered by one structural proof, so the result is not an arbitrary finite table or small numerical gain.
